title_en: Li Yandong v. Shanghai Hanyu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd. — dispute over intermediary contract
ruling_gist_en: In house sale intermediation activities, an intermediary company (intermediary) shall, in respect of the entrusted matters and intermediary services, assume the duty of care commensurate with that of a professional entity, and shall focus on examining and verifying the authenticity of the certification materials related to the transaction, such as the identities of the parties, property ownership, entrustment and agency, credit and financial standing, etc. If the intermediary company fails to exercise the necessary duty of care and thus fails to discover significant defects or deficiencies in the relevant materials provided by one party, thereby causing the other party to suffer losses due to fraud, it shall bear compensation liability within the corresponding scope according to its degree of fault.
keywords_en: Civil; Intermediary contract dispute; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Shanghai Municipality; Natural person; Legal person; Contract Law; Duty of care of the intermediary; Scope of compensation liability; Sharing of deposit loss; Partially upheld; House sale intermediation; Forged notarial certificate; Dual sale of the same property; Deposit payment; Good faith; Contract dispute; House sale; Consulting company limited intermediary contract dispute
full_text_en:
Li Yandong v. Shanghai Hanyu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd. — dispute over intermediary contract

【Ruling Summary】

In a house sale intermediary activity, the intermediary company (the intermediary) shall bear a duty of care that meets the requirements of a professional entity for the entrusted matters and intermediary services, paying attention to verifying the authenticity of evidentiary materials related to the transaction, such as the identity of the parties, property ownership, agency authority, creditworthiness, etc. If the intermediary company fails to fulfill the necessary duty of care and thus fails to discover significant defects or deficiencies in the relevant materials provided by one party, thereby causing the other party to be defrauded and suffer losses, it shall bear compensation liability within the corresponding scope according to its degree of fault.

Plaintiff: Li Yandong, male, 29 years old, Han Chinese, residing in Bao'an District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Defendant: Shanghai Hanyu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd., domiciled at Anting Town, Jiading District, Shanghai City, actual place of business: Zhaojiabang Road, Xuhui District, Shanghai City.

Legal Representative: Shi Shaoming, Chairman of the Company.

The plaintiff, Li Yandong, filed a lawsuit with the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendant, Shanghai Hanyu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hanyu Real Estate), concerning a dispute over an intermediary contract.

The plaintiff, Li Yandong, alleged that: On March 7, 2012, through the intermediary introduction of the defendant, Hanyu Real Estate, he reached a sale agreement with third parties Zhou Min, Cai Fang, and Chen Bingyu for the house located at Room 301, Building 4, Lane 6869, Shangnan Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai (hereinafter referred to as the disputed house). On the same day, he paid a deposit of RMB 200,000 to Zhou Min through the account of his spouse, Liu Mingming, and agreed on the payment method for the balance and the transfer date, etc. On March 8, 2012, he discovered that the disputed house had already been successfully traded on March 2, 2012. The notarial certificate held by Zhou Min was forged. Therefore, on March 14, 2012, he reported the case to the Zhoupu Police Station of the Pudong Branch of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau. After the public security organs filed the case for investigation, Zhou Min was criminally detained. Li Yandong believed that Hanyu Real Estate, as a professional intermediary institution, should fulfill its basic duty of review and investigation when providing professional house intermediary services. However, Hanyu Real Estate failed to investigate whether the disputed house had already been sold, the precise information of the principal and the agent, and the clarity of the property ownership, causing him huge losses. Hanyu Real Estate should bear liability for gross negligence. He requested the court to order Hanyu Real Estate to compensate for losses of RMB 200,000.

The defendant, Hanyu Real Estate, argued that: The plaintiff, Li Yandong, did not pay the deposit of RMB 200,000 to the third party Zhou Min through the defendant. Instead, Li Yandong paid it directly to Zhou Min. This loss is unrelated to the defendant, and Li Yandong should claim the loss from Zhou Min. When the defendant conducted the intermediary activity, the disputed house was still under the names of Zhou Min and others, and it was available for trading. Moreover, Li Yandong had also seen the property ownership certificate when signing the agreement. Therefore, the defendant had fulfilled its relevant review and investigation obligations. It requested the court to dismiss Li Yandong's claims.

The Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai found the following facts in the first instance:

On March 7, 2012, the plaintiff, Li Yandong, the defendant, Hanyu Real Estate, and the third party, Zhou Min, signed a "Real Estate Sale Intermediary Agreement", stipulating that through the intermediary introduction of Hanyu Real Estate, Li Yandong would purchase from Zhou Min the house located at Room 301, Building 4, Lane 6869, Shangnan Road, Kangqiao Town, Pudong New Area, Shanghai, with a total price of RMB 1,180,000. On the same day, the three parties signed a "Real Estate Sale Agreement", stipulating that the total deposit was RMB 200,000, and Zhou Min entrusted Hanyu Real Estate to collect and keep the deposit on his behalf. After Zhou Min delivered the property ownership certificate and other document proofs to Hanyu Real Estate for safekeeping on the date of signing the agreement, Zhou Min could retrieve the deposit kept by Hanyu Real Estate. The above agreements also made provisions on other matters. On the same day, Li Yandong paid a deposit of RMB 200,000 to Zhou Min through the account of his spouse, Liu Mingming. On the same day, Zhou Min issued a deposit receipt to Li Yandong, confirming receipt of the deposit of RMB 200,000 from Li Yandong. On March 14, 2012, Li Yandong reported to the public security organ, stating that on March 7, 2012, he signed a house sale agreement with Zhou Min through Hanyu Real Estate and paid a deposit of RMB 200,000 to Zhou Min by bank transfer, intending to purchase the house at Room 301, Building 4, Lane 6869, Shangnan Road, Pudong New Area, Shanghai. Later, he found that the notarial certificate provided by Zhou Min was forged and suspected fraud. On March 17, 2012, the Pudong Branch of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau filed a case for investigation into Zhou Min's suspected contract fraud. On October 17, 2012, Zhou Min was sentenced to eight years' imprisonment, fined RMB 60,000, and ordered to return the criminal gains to the victim banks and the victim (i.e., Li Yandong) by the Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai for the crimes of credit card fraud and contract fraud. After the judgment, Zhou Min appealed. On December 14, 2012, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court ruled to reject the appeal and uphold the original judgment.

The disputed house was originally jointly owned by the third parties Zhou Min, Zhou Guozuo, Cai Fang, and Chen Bingyu, with Zhou Min holding a one-sixth share. During the transaction of the disputed house, Zhou Min once issued a notarial certificate to Li Yandong and Hanyu Real Estate, stating that Zhou Guozuo, Cai Fang, and Chen Bingyu authorized Zhou Min to handle matters related to the transaction of the disputed house on their behalf. This notarial certificate was later confirmed to be forged by the Shanghai Guoxin Notary Public Office. The Pudong New Area Real Estate Registration Office of Shanghai accepted the transfer of ownership of the disputed house on March 30, 2012. On April 16, 2012, the house was transferred to the names of the third parties Xia Guihua, Shen Xiaofang, and Xia Yuhao. On April 9, 2012, during this period, the mortgage on the disputed house was cancelled.

The Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai reasoned in the first instance:

The defendant, Hanyu Real Estate, as a professional house intermediary institution, should fulfill necessary and prudent review and verification obligations when conducting intermediary services, such as verifying source information, verifying the identity of the seller, and assessing the reasonableness of the transaction process. The buyer also has a duty of care for the house transaction. In this case, although Hanyu Real Estate conducted certain investigations, verifications, etc., it failed to investigate and verify whether the disputed house was subject to double sale, whether the notarial certificate was forged, etc., resulting in the loss of the deposit paid by the plaintiff, Li Yandong. Moreover, Li Yandong did not deliver the deposit to Hanyu Real Estate for safekeeping as agreed but paid it directly to Zhou Min, and also failed to exercise due diligence regarding the authenticity of the notarial certificate, resulting in the inability to recover the deposit. Both parties were at fault in this process and should bear corresponding liabilities respectively. Since Zhou Min has been sentenced and ordered to return the criminal gains, considering the degree of fault of both Li Yandong and Hanyu Real Estate, the court determines that Hanyu Real Estate shall bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of RMB 30,000.

Accordingly, the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai, pursuant to Article 60 and Article 425 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, on January 23, 2013, rendered the following judgment:

The defendant, Shanghai Hanyu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd., shall compensate the plaintiff, Li Yandong, for losses within the scope of RMB 30,000 for the portion of the criminal restitution owed by the third party Zhou Min that remains unpaid. This amount shall be paid within ten days from the date of suspension or termination of the criminal restitution execution.

Li Yandong, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court.

Li Yandong appealed, arguing that: At the request of the intermediary company's staff member Zhou Honglin, he paid the deposit directly to Zhou Min, the intermediary issued a receipt, and the three parties went to the bank together for the transfer. He did not arbitrarily and without reason pay the deposit directly to Zhou Min; he paid the deposit only after the intermediary company requested it and gave a positive affirmation regarding the safety of the house transaction. He confirmed the relevant documents provided by the seller and signed the sale agreement only after the intermediary company gave a positive affirmation of safety. However, Hanyu Real Estate, in order to secure the sale agreement, deliberately fabricated false facts, made misleading false propaganda to gain his trust and earn intermediary fees, and was seriously negligent. Hanyu Real Estate, as a professional intermediary company, failed to fulfill its basic obligations, causing him huge losses, and should bear full responsibility. Accordingly, he requested the revocation of the original judgment and a judgment in favor of his original claim.

Hanyu Real Estate also appealed against the first-instance judgment, arguing that: Li Yandong paid the deposit directly to Zhou Min, and Zhou Min issued a receipt; neither party proposed that the deposit be kept by the defendant. Li Yandong's extremely careless attitude in the transaction led to the current consequences, and he was grossly negligent. The defendant, as the intermediary, could not verify the authenticity of the notarial certificate, and Zhou Min provided the original notarial certificate, which formally met the basic requirements of a notarial certificate. As for the issue of double sale, the defendant could not verify it, and it should not normally be possible to learn whether a house had been sold through a property rights information inquiry. This transaction resulted from Zhou Min's subjective malicious fraud and concealment, and the defendant had fulfilled its intermediary obligations. Accordingly, it requested the revocation of the original judgment and a judgment dismissing Li Yandong's original claim.

After the second instance trial, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

Further found that, in the forged notarial certificate, the date of birth of Cai Fang stated therein was inconsistent with the one recorded in her identity card number. Neither party mentioned this fact in the first instance.

In the second instance, the appellant Li Yandong stated that: Zhou Min held the original household registration booklet and the original identity cards of Zhou Min himself and Cai Fang, and they went to the police station with him and Hanyu Real Estate to verify; the household registration booklet and identity cards were all genuine. Along with the original household registration booklet and identity cards, Zhou Min provided the power of attorney. After verbal verification, he orally raised objections to the problems existing in the notarial certificate. Before payment, Zhou Honglin of Hanyu Real Estate said that he had already confirmed it. He asked the intermediary to confirm, and the intermediary said that confirmation could only be done at the notary public office on site. He then called to confirm, but the notary public office stated that they did not accept telephone inquiries and that on-site confirmation was necessary. Since the notary public office's response was consistent with what Zhou Honglin had said earlier, and Zhou Honglin assured him that he had already confirmed it, he did not go to the site for confirmation. The appellant Li Yandong stated that he requested the court of second instance to amend the judgment so that Hanyu Real Estate would bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of RMB 100,000.

In the second instance, on March 27, 2013, Hanyu Real Estate applied to withdraw its appeal. On April 17, 2013, the court requested Hanyu Real Estate to notify its staff member Zhou Honglin to appear in court as a witness. The witness Zhou Honglin testified that he did not have broker qualifications and did not discover the problems in the notarial certificate. He did not go to the notary public office to verify the authenticity of the notarial certificate on site; he personally thought it was genuine. The notary public office did not accept telephone inquiries; on-site verification could be done by bringing the identity card and the original notarial certificate to the notary public office. When signing the intermediary contract, both Zhou Min and Cai Fang were present; he did not ask Zhou Min about the double sale situation. In practice, the deposit was directly transferred to the upper party (seller), and the deposit clauses in the intermediary contract were basically not used. On the day Li Yandong paid the deposit, in order to withdraw cash, Zhou Min transferred RMB 20,000 each to him (Zhou Honglin) and Li Yandong to help Zhou Min withdraw cash.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court reasoned in the second instance:

The appellant Hanyu Real Estate's application to withdraw its appeal is not contrary to the law and is hereby permitted. Based on the facts found, the appellant Li Yandong was the victim of the contract fraud committed by Zhou Min. Zhou Min defrauded Li Yandong of the RMB 200,000 deposit paid for the house purchase. Zhou Min's criminal gains shall be recovered and returned to the victim. The first-instance court's decision that Hanyu Real Estate shall bear supplementary compensation liability is consistent with the facts of the case, and the second instance affirms this.

The main dispute in this second instance is the scope of Hanyu Real Estate's supplementary compensation liability, which should be determined comprehensively based on the circumstances of the case. According to the facts found in the second instance, the date of birth of Cai Fang stated in the forged notarial certificate was inconsistent with the one recorded in her identity card number. This matter can be determined without the need for professional knowledge. Given that the notary public office could not provide telephone verification of authenticity, Hanyu Real Estate should have gone to the notary public office to conduct on-site verification, but it failed to take such measures. Moreover, according to the appellant Li Yandong's statement during the second instance, he had noticed the problems in the notarial certificate before payment and raised objections. Li Yandong had ample opportunity to actively verify the authenticity of the notarial certificate before making the payment. Since both Li Yandong and Hanyu Real Estate failed to fulfill the aforementioned duty of prudence, Li Yandong himself became the victim of Zhou Min's contract fraud. Hanyu Real Estate, as an entity specialized in intermediary activities, should do its utmost to safeguard the interests of the principal in carrying out its business operations. According to the facts found, the staff member handling this intermediary business for Hanyu Real Estate did not have broker qualifications, failed to seriously verify that the disputed house had already been sold, and did not strictly fulfill the deposit safekeeping obligation as stipulated in the contract, enabling the third party Zhou Min to commit fraud and thereby causing losses to Li Yandong. Considering the above circumstances, Li Yandong's request that Hanyu Real Estate bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of RMB 100,000 is reasonable and can be supported. The first-instance judgment shall be adjusted accordingly.

In conclusion, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 170 and Article 175 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on May 9, 2013, rendered the following judgment:

The amount in the civil judgment (2012) Ji Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 809 of the Jiading District People's Court of Shanghai is amended as follows: Shanghai Hanyu Real Estate Consulting Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, bear supplementary compensation liability to Li Yandong within the scope of RMB 100,000 for the portion of the criminal restitution owed by the third party Zhou Min that remains unpaid.

This judgment is final.
